country_profile.name: The shape of Ardenia
country_profile.body: Ardenia is a small country that behaves like a large one because it has never been left alone: roughly 78,000 square kilometres and 6.4 million people on paper, closer to 6.0 million given who has left. A mountain wall in the north descends through a chain of basins toward the Aster Sea in the west. The long eastern frontier is easier to cross than the mountains and harder to ignore. Its politics is chiefly the argument among the nine regions laid across that geography.

kesla.name: The Kesla
kesla.body: The Kesla rises in the northern mountains, bends through Karsen and Vashtera, and reaches the western sea near Tavri. Ardenians locate more than places by it: above the Kesla means highland, poor, devout and Ardenian-speaking; below it means the plain, the towns and the mixed places.

ceasefire_line.name: The Vetrenka ceasefire line
ceasefire_line.body: Since autumn 1992 the Vetrenka Free Front has administered the land behind a ceasefire line Ardenia does not recognise and cannot cross. Together with the ungoverned uplands of Anera, roughly a fifth of the map does not answer to Vashtera.

regions.name: Vashtera Capital District
regions.body: The capital and the belt of dormitory towns the Union built around it hold 1.1 million people, a sixth of the country, and effectively all of its media, ministries, courts, foreign embassies and hard currency. What Vashtera decides is not what the country experiences, and every party outside it says so constantly.

regions.name: Zavost
regions.body: The eastern industrial province was built between 1948 and 1974 for Union demand that no longer exists: steel, rail rolling stock, fertiliser and nitrogen works. Kolvenian-speakers are a plurality in its cities. Zavost has the country's highest unemployment, its largest body of skilled workers, its only real trade unions, and the border with Krasova.

regions.name: Darev
regions.body: Darev is the republic's long eastern shoulder: dry market towns, military roads and energy installations pressed between Zavost and the Krasovan and Merovan frontiers. Vashtera calls it a strategic corridor. The people who live there call it the place every army crosses and every ministry remembers after the road has closed.

regions.name: The Sela
regions.body: The central plain grows grain, sunflower and sugar beet. Its 340,000 hectares of collective farmland were legally dissolved in 1991 and have been physically contested ever since. This is Agrarian Union country; it votes on credit terms, fuel prices and roads, in that order, with little visible interest in anything else.

regions.name: Anera
regions.body: The western and north-western highlands are stone villages, sheep, orchards, monasteries and remittances. Anera is the poorest and most homogeneously Ardenian region, with the highest church attendance and the most rifles. It is Dorin Vasca's home. The capital appoints officials there; they are received politely and largely ignored.

regions.name: Karsen
regions.body: Karsen holds the north-central passes and the upper Kesla. Its valleys contain hydro stations, garrison towns and communities that can reach Vashtera in an afternoon when the road is open and not at all when it is not. Control belongs formally to the republic and practically to whoever keeps the pass, the transformer and the depot working.

regions.name: The Kelvet Coast
regions.body: The south-western approaches hold Tavri, the main loyalist port, the fishing fleet, customs houses and container yards. Roughly nine-tenths of Ardenia's legal trade and effectively all of its illegal trade passes here. The Falcons were born on Kelvet, and nobody who governs Ardenia gets to be squeamish about Tavri.

regions.name: Orvena
regions.body: Orvena is the loyalist western hinge between the central basin and the Vetrenka line. Foothill farms, displaced families, Selvara's small harbour and the only dependable road around the closed coast give it more strategic weight than its population suggests. Every proposal for Vetrenka begins by asking what Orvena can carry.

regions.name: Vetrenka
regions.body: The western coastal strip is twelve per cent of the map, three per cent of the population, and about a third of the useful coastline. It has held autonomy under three sovereigns, speaks a distinct dialect, and has shown no great attachment to Ardenia in two centuries. It is now governed by the Vetrenka Free Front.

cities.name: Vashtera
cities.body: Vashtera sits where the Kesla leaves the hills: a Verdan-era core of yellow stucco and ministries, Kestrel Square before the Chamber, a Union ring of eleven-storey blocks, and currency kiosks on every central corner. Heat has been unreliable for two winters and the trams run when the depot has fuel. It is the whole of the state's capacity and roughly a quarter of its problems.

cities.name: Duvinsk / Duvin
cities.body: Zavost's principal city, about 340,000 people, is a company town for a country that no longer has the company. It was Duvin before 1938 and is officially Duvinsk now; which name a speaker chooses tells everyone in the room how they vote.

cities.name: Tavri
cities.body: The second city, about 290,000 people, is older, warmer and richer than it declares. Its Osmene-era quarter and Muslim community predate the Ardenian state; its customs house runs the country's actual balance of payments.

cities.name: Rovets
cities.body: The Sela's largest market town, about 95,000 people, is a grain exchange, a line of silos, and the Agrarian Union's real capital.

cities.name: Kavor
cities.body: A market town of roughly 40,000 beneath a monastery, Kavor is the last place on the western road where the government's writ is unambiguous.

cities.name: Ostrena
cities.body: Vetrenka's capital is a port of roughly 55,000 that the Ardenian state has not entered since September 1992.

cities.name: Karvel
cities.body: Karvel guards the highest year-round approach to the northern passes. It is a garrison, a livestock market and a queue of lorries waiting for weather, paperwork or both to clear.

cities.name: Lestara
cities.body: Lestara is the upper Kesla rail junction, built where the gorge allows one bridge and therefore gives one station master an implausible amount of influence over the capital's supplies.

cities.name: Ordel
cities.body: Ordel is a foothill market swollen by families from the ceasefire districts. Warehouses, aid offices and transport cooperatives have made a temporary town into Orvena's administrative centre.

cities.name: Selvara
cities.body: Selvara's harbour is shallow, crowded and loyal. It cannot replace Tavri, but during a closure or confrontation it is the western outlet the government can still reach without crossing the Vetrenka line.

cities.name: Meradin
cities.body: Meradin is Darev's frontier garrison and caravan market. The army, customs service and three languages share its main street while disagreeing about who has authority beyond it.

cities.name: Azren
cities.body: Azren grew around the eastern compressor station and the workers who keep the Zovar line moving. Energy policy is not abstract there: it is the shift roster, the border gate and the town heating system.
